decisions.reason: The local natural-number convention includes zero, but the Fourier basis and ellipsoid start at one. The original A_p has no defined zero-coordinate multiplier, and discarding that coordinate would destroy injectivity and the definition of G dagger. Explicitly defining the real positive-index ell^2 space repairs the model without changing its intended rates or quantifiers.

With zero-based coordinates the multiplier 0^(-p) is undefined. Even if a zero-coordinate observation were supplied separately, the prescribed zero output would leave an arbitrary theta_0 uncontrolled by the positive-index ellipsoid, invalidating the bound. Explicitly taking the real sequence space on positive indices eliminates that extra coordinate and makes the original complete estimate valid.

reviews.reason: On explicitly positive real sequence indices every j^(-p) is defined, bounded by one, and nonzero. Thus A_p maps ell^2 to itself injectively and G dagger is single-valued on its image. The weighted ellipsoid has uniformly vanishing tails, so its stated compact-domain interpretation remains sound. Fourier lift, finite multipliers and Lipschitz layers map L^2 to L^2; the existing nonempty-selector assumption and empty-class convention remain explicit. The odd-mesh status claim matches the supplied local example. Updated only the formulation and its owning manifest/contract mirrors; no proof or solution is claimed.

All sequence indices are now explicitly positive. For 1<=j<=m the reconstruction error is j^p eta_j, whose norm is at most m^p delta. For j>m the weighted constraint bounds the tail norm by R(m+1)^(-s). The triangle inequality yields exactly the original bound, including m=1, zero noise and zero truth. No new supplier or choice principle is required; the three proof steps, their tags and bound remain unchanged. The owning manifest mirrors the corrected Example, and its existing proof contract already explicitly states positive coordinates.
